samples.summary: `backend.md` says the browser `state` is `w.<HMAC(JWT_SECRET, value)>`, contradicting the same document and the implementation, which HKDF-derive a separate key
samples.evidence: Line 110 states the state is `w.<HMAC(JWT_SECRET, value)>`. Later in the same file (the "That published pair is also why the binding is **not** signed with `JWT_SECRET`" paragraph, ~line 400) and `bindingSecret()` in `github-auth.guard.ts` both say the key is HKDF-derived from `JWT_SECRET` (or `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET`), explicitly not `JWT_SECRET` itself. A reader of the API section is told the opposite of the security rationale section.

samples.summary: `secretEquals` is defined twice inside `packages/backend/src/auth` (and a third constant-time compare exists elsewhere in the backend)

samples.summary: `github-auth.guard.ts` has become the app's cookie-policy and key-derivation module; the controller imports 14 symbols from a file named after a guard, including the *session* cookie predicate
samples.evidence: The file now exports `secureCookies`, `loginCookieName`, `loginCookieOptions`, `loginCookieValues`, `joinLoginCookieValues`, `secretEquals`, `bindingSecret`, `stateSignature`, `consentToken`, `resetSecureCookieWarning`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_LOGINS`, cookie-name constants and `STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS`. `auth.controller.ts` imports all of these, and uses `secureCookies` for `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` — session-cookie policy now lives in a GitHub OAuth guard. A `cookie-policy.ts` / `login-binding.ts` module beside the guard would match the layer these concerns actually belong to.

samples.summary: `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` duplicates route knowledge that lives in the controllers, with nothing linking the two

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `COOKIE_SECURE` is a real, highest-precedence config input to `secureCookies()` (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:80-89, 158-160) governing the Secure flag on session, refresh and all three login cookies, and it is documented operator-side (packages/backend/README.md:39-51; packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:136). A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for cookie[_ ]?secure over docs/ finds it in no design doc at all — only docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-lessons.md:161,164, a task-lessons file. The canonical backend env table (docs/design/backend.md:681-700) was extended in this area with OAUTH_STATE_SECRET (:687) and a rewritten NODE_ENV row (:696) yet omits COOKIE_SECURE, and the accompanying prose at :371-378 affirmatively states every cookie's Secure flag comes from GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL's scheme with NODE_ENV as the only fallback — a description the shipped override contradicts. I considered refuting on the grounds that the table is non-exhaustive (FILE_STORAGE_PREFIX, YORKIE_SECRET_KEY are absent), but those vars are documented in their own area design docs (docs/design/pdf.md:102, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:229, docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:49), which confirms rather than refutes the convention: COOKIE_SECURE's area doc is backend.md § Cookie Configuration, and there is no deferral note pointing env docs at the README. No counterexample exists.

I searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide case-insensitive grep for COOKIE_SECURE returns no file under docs/design/ (only packages/backend/README.md:39, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:136, the auth sources/spec, .agent-review artifacts, and docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-lessons.md:161,164); a concept-level grep across docs/design for cookie_secure / "explicit override … secure" / "operator … secure" found nothing.
